library(EpiModel)

## Introduction

The *Working with Model Parameters* vignette shows how to define scenarios with `create_scenario_list()` and run one with `use_scenario()`. Research projects usually run many scenarios, each with many replicates, and often start them all from the end of a calibrated burn-in period. This vignette covers the functions for that workflow:

- `netsim_scenarios()` runs every scenario of a list in batches of simulations and saves each batch to a file.
- `get_scenarios_batches_infos()`, `merge_netsim_scenarios()`, `merge_netsim_scenarios_tibble()` and `get_scenarios_tibble_infos()` list and merge these files.
- `make_restart_pool()` turns chosen simulations into a pool of restart points, `validate_restart_pool()` checks it, and `netsim_path_wrapper()` runs simulations from it.

The same code runs on a SLURM cluster through the `slurmworkflow` step templates of the [EpiModelHPC](https://github.com/EpiModel/EpiModelHPC) package, such as `step_tmpl_netsim_scenarios()`.

## Setup

The scenario functions read the starting point of the simulations from a file, so the fitted network model is saved with `saveRDS()`. Everything here is written under a temporary directory.

```{r setup, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
set.seed(10)

work_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "scenarios-vignette")
dir.create(work_dir)

nw <- network_initialize(n = 200)
est <- netest(nw,
  formation = ~edges, target.stats = 60,
  coef.diss = dissolution_coefs(~offset(edges), 10, 0),
  verbose = FALSE
)
est_path <- file.path(work_dir, "est.rds")
saveRDS(est, est_path)

param <- param.net(inf.prob = 0.5, rec.rate = 0.05, act.rate = 1)
init <- init.net(i.num = 10)
control <- control.net(
  type = "SIS", nsteps = 50,
  tergmLite = TRUE, resimulate.network = TRUE, save.run = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

`tergmLite = TRUE` and `save.run = TRUE` keep the state needed to restart the simulations later, which the restart pool section uses.

## Running Scenarios in Batches

`netsim_scenarios()` runs `n_rep` simulations of each scenario, in batches of up to `n_cores` simulations. The simulations of a batch run in parallel, each as its own `netsim()` call, and the batch is saved as `sim__<scenario>__<batch>.rds` in `output_dir`. Here, 4 simulations on 2 cores make 2 batches per scenario.

By default the simulations run on `future::plan("multisession", workers = n_cores)`. Another plan can be set with `future::tweak()` in `control$future.use.plan`. This vignette uses a sequential plan, so that it starts no R sessions.

```{r run_scenarios}
control$future.use.plan <- future::tweak(future::sequential)

scenarios.df <- data.frame(
  .scenario.id = c("base", "low_inf"),
  .at = 1,
  inf.prob = c(0.5, 0.2)
)
scenarios.list <- create_scenario_list(scenarios.df)

sims_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "sims")
netsim_scenarios(
  path_to_x = est_path,
  param = param,
  init = init,
  control = control,
  scenarios_list = scenarios.list,
  n_rep = 4,
  n_cores = 2,
  output_dir = sims_dir
)
```

With a `multisession` plan, each simulation runs in a separate R session that has neither the global objects nor the attached packages of the current one. Modules written in a script must therefore call package functions with `pkg::fun()`. See the Parallel Simulation section of `?netsim`.

## Listing and Merging the Batches

`get_scenarios_batches_infos()` lists the batch files with their scenario and batch number.

```{r batches_infos}
get_scenarios_batches_infos(sims_dir)
```

`merge_netsim_scenarios()` merges the batches of each scenario into a single `netsim` object, saved as `merged__<scenario>.rds`.

```{r merge}
merged_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "merged")
merge_netsim_scenarios(sims_dir, merged_dir)
sim_base <- readRDS(file.path(merged_dir, "merged__base.rds"))
sim_base
```

For analysis, `merge_netsim_scenarios_tibble()` saves the epidemic output of each scenario as a `data.frame`, `df__<scenario>.rds`, with the `batch_number`, `sim_number` (the position of the simulation within its batch) and `sim` (over the whole scenario) columns first. `steps_to_keep` keeps only the last time steps, and `cols` only some columns. `get_scenarios_tibble_infos()` lists the files.

```{r merge_tibble}
tibbles_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "tibbles")
merge_netsim_scenarios_tibble(
  sim_dir = sims_dir,
  output_dir = tibbles_dir,
  steps_to_keep = 50
)
infos <- get_scenarios_tibble_infos(tibbles_dir)
infos

d <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(infos$file_path, readRDS), .id = "scenario")
d$scenario <- infos$scenario_name[as.integer(d$scenario)]
d_end <- d[d$time == 50, ]
aggregate(i.num ~ scenario, data = d_end, FUN = mean)
```

## Restart Pools

A common design runs a burn-in once, for example the calibrated model up to the start of an intervention, and starts every scenario from its end. Restarting all the scenarios from the same set of simulations also makes them comparable simulation by simulation.

### Making a Pool

`make_restart_pool()` builds a pool from the batch files of a run: pool element `i` is made from row `i` of `keep_sims`, a `data.frame` with the `batch_number` and `sim_number` of the simulations to keep. Each element is a single simulation restart point made with `make_restart_point()`, which keeps only the last time step and makes it step 1. Attributes holding time steps are shifted to match: the core ones (`entrTime`, `exitTime` and `infTime`) always are, and `time_attrs` lists the model's other ones, such as the time of diagnosis in most extension models. This model has none, hence `c()`. Here, the pool is made from the 4 simulations of the `"base"` scenario.

```{r make_pool}
keep_sims <- unique(d[d$scenario == "base", c("batch_number", "sim_number")])
keep_sims

pool_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "pool")
make_restart_pool(
  pool_dir = pool_dir,
  scenarios_dir = sims_dir,
  scenario_name = "base",
  keep_sims = keep_sims,
  time_attrs = c()
)
list.files(pool_dir)
```

`validate_restart_pool()` checks a pool before a long run: that every element exists, holds a single simulation that `netsim()` can restart from, was made with the installed major.minor version of EpiModel, and keeps the same number of time steps as the others.

```{r validate_pool}
pool_infos <- validate_restart_pool(pool_dir)
pool_infos[, c("pool_num", "n_runs", "nsteps", "epimodel_version")]
```

### Running Scenarios From a Pool

A pool directory is passed as `path_to_x`. Simulation `k` of each scenario starts from pool element `(k - 1) %% N + 1` for a pool of `N` elements, so simulation `k` starts from the same element in every scenario, and the pool is reused in order when there are more simulations than elements.

The elements keep a single time step, so the restarted simulations start at `start = 2`. Here they run 25 more time steps.

```{r run_from_pool, message = FALSE}
control_restart <- control.net(
  type = "SIS", start = 2, nsteps = 26,
  tergmLite = TRUE, resimulate.network = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE
)
control_restart$future.use.plan <- future::tweak(future::sequential)

restart_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "sims_restart")
netsim_scenarios(
  path_to_x = pool_dir,
  param = param,
  init = init,
  control = control_restart,
  scenarios_list = scenarios.list,
  n_rep = 4,
  n_cores = 2,
  output_dir = restart_dir
)
get_scenarios_batches_infos(restart_dir)
```

`netsim_scenarios()` runs each batch with `netsim_path_wrapper()`, which can also be called directly to run some simulations from a pool or from a single file. It returns a list of `netsim` objects with one simulation each, and records the restart point used.

```{r path_wrapper}
sims <- netsim_path_wrapper(
  path_to_x = pool_dir,
  param = param,
  init = init,
  control = control_restart,
  sim_nums = 1:2
)
sims[[2]]$restart_point
```

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
unlink(work_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```
